chunk_findings.detail: `_step` only consults `mid_gate` inside `if held is not None:`, but `_with_session` passes `held_live=None` for any lane without a live lease while still passing the lane’s `mid_gate` from `_mid_gates`. The new `Lane.step` field doc says the step is the in-flight gate (`mid_gate`) first, and the existing `mid_gate` field is documented as the step a stopped lane/corpse names. Given a stopped lane whose lease is gone (`_held` returns `None`) but whose `_mid_gates` entry is `"research"` and whose `f.last_kind` is `"heartbeat"`, `_step` returns `"heartbeat"`, so `ddflow lanes` STEP shows `heartbeat` instead of the gate that was in flight when the lane stopped.

data.probe: confirmed: renamed _step to consult mid_gate first (before the held-item branch), so a released/stopped lane with an in-flight gate.started shows that gate; regression test test_step_names_the_gate_a_released_lane_was_on_when_it_left asserts step=='research'. Fixed in commit 4e0df8e72.

chunk_findings.detail: `_ledger` passes `held_live` to `_with_session`, but `_with_session` defines its parameter as `held` rather than `held_live`. When `held` is `None` (because a lane holds an item without an active lease or no item at all), `held_live` is `None`, which is then passed to `_step` where it is checked as `if held is not None:`. This causes a lane holding an item without an active lease to incorrectly have its step evaluated using `_next_gate(held, cfg)` instead of falling back to `f.last_kind`, violating the logic that a finished or released item is not held.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lanes/ledger.py:270

data.probe: refuted: _with_session's parameter is named held but receives held_live (the ternary: held if (held is not None and held.lease is not None) else None), so a lane holding an item with NO active lease passes None and _step's 'if held is not None' is False -> returns f.last_kind. Probe: a lane that claims X then releases shows step=='lease.released', not _next_gate. No code change: the guard is already correct.
